text: Address the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2028 offer-and-sale restriction before it applies to a venue's pairing of a payment stablecoin. With Treasury, state before July 18, 2028 how the GENIUS Act's offer-and-sale restriction applies to a venue's pairing of a payment stablecoin, and in the meantime require the Notice to identify, for each paired payment stablecoin, whether its issuer is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer. From that date, subject to exceptions, the Act makes it unlawful for a digital asset service provider to offer or sell a payment stablecoin to a person in the United States unless a permitted payment stablecoin issuer issued it. The date falls inside the Order's term, which runs to September 17, 2031, and a footnote to the Order leaves open whether a venue is a digital asset service provider. The comment does not ask the Commission to limit paired assets by type.

letter_title: SEC Transfer Agent Rules
ask: State which record governs, reconcile on-chain supply to the master securityholder file every business day, and count excess supply in the overissuance test
text: State which record governs, reconcile on-chain supply to the master securityholder file every business day, and count excess supply in the overissuance test. Require the recordkeeping transfer agent, for each tokenized issue, to designate in writing whether the crypto network is the master securityholder file, a component of it, or a copy, and which record governs if they disagree, and to disclose that designation to holders. Add to the rule's definition of a record difference the case where the quantity of a tokenized issue outstanding on any crypto network differs from the quantity the file records, reconciled at least every business day, so that a difference left unresolved is reported as an aged record difference. Count units outstanding on a network in excess of the file in the overissuance test, and extend the duty to resolve an overissuance to such supply, whoever created it. Decline the exemption the SEC's question floats for a file kept exclusively on an immutable blockchain network: a public ledger's history persists only while the network and its archive nodes do. As proposed, tokens minted beyond the file, by an exploit, a bridge to another network or an error, are neither a record difference nor an overissuance, although monitoring for overissuance is one of a transfer agent's statutory functions.

letter_title: SEC Transfer Agent Rules
ask: Define exclusive control of a ledger component as sole authority to create, cancel, or freeze units or move them without the holder's authorization, held by the transfer agent or exercised only on its instruction, under joint authorization
text: Define exclusive control of a ledger component as sole authority to create, cancel, or freeze units or move them without the holder's authorization, held by the transfer agent or exercised only on its instruction, under joint authorization. The rule requires the transfer agent to keep "exclusive control" over the master securityholder file but does not define the term, and the release reads the ability to view a ledger and furnish copies as independent access; anyone can view and copy a public ledger. Define exclusive control, for any component of the file kept on a crypto network, as sole authority to create, cancel or freeze units, or to transfer them without the holder's authorization, held by the transfer agent or by a person acting only on its instruction under an agreement the transfer agent can terminate, and exercised under joint authorization of at least two persons it designates. Holders would still transfer their own units. The joint-authorization element follows the Commission's own custody proposal for advisers, and the standard parallels the control test the OCC adopted for custody under the GENIUS Act. Where a person other than the transfer agent can freeze or move units at the level of the network, as the Arbitrum Security Council did in emergency responses to two exploits in 2026, the transfer agent should identify that person to holders, and that network should carry only a copy of the record, with the off-chain file governing.

letter_title: SEC Transfer Agent Rules
ask: Treat the privileged functions of a token as transfer agent functions
text: Treat the privileged functions of a token as transfer agent functions. The rule text records the results of a token's privileged functions, in the transfer journal's issuances, cancellations and transfers, but never names the functions or says who holds them. Require that each privileged function of a tokenized issue's own contract be held by the recordkeeping transfer agent or be exercisable only on its instruction; require issuer authorization for every creation or cancellation of units, as the transfer agent rules already require for changes to the control book; require joint authorization and a transfer journal entry for every use of a privileged function, including freezes, pauses and changes to the contract's logic, recording any instruction or legal order the use rests on; require disclosure to holders of which persons hold which functions; confirm that a resale restriction enforced in a token contract is a restrictive legend under the proposed rule on restrictive legends, so that lifting it is a removal subject to the rule; and name these functions in any guidance on what makes a risk material under the comprehensive risk management rule. These are transfer agent functions in fact; the rule should make them transfer agent functions in law.
topics: custody and collateral disclosure and reporting
refs: Questions 50, 84, 109 and 140; rule 17ad-10(e); proposed rule 17ad-31; rule 17ad-12(a)(2)

letter_title: SEC Transfer Agent Rules
ask: Hand over control with the records, and plan for a transfer agent's failure
text: Hand over control with the records, and plan for a transfer agent's failure. The proposal requires a departing transfer agent to deliver its records within fifteen calendar days. For a tokenized issue, records are not enough: a successor that receives the records but not the privileged roles of the token contract cannot correct, reissue or move units, and a withheld key gives a departing transfer agent the same leverage a withheld file does. Require the handover to include every privileged role and key the transfer agent holds or controls for each tokenized issue, or their revocation and reissue to the successor; require the business continuity plan the comprehensive risk management rule calls for to address network halts and forks, contract exploits, bridge failures, and loss or compromise of keys; and keep the rule that there can be only one recordkeeping transfer agent for an issue, applied across networks, so that one transfer agent is accountable for reconciling every representation of the issue. The release reports that of the 144 transfer agents that withdrew from registration between 2016 and 2025, 56 (39 percent) indicated a successor transfer agent for each issue; in a concentrated market, one transfer agent's failure can reach many tokenized issues at once.

letter_title: SEC Transfer Agent Rules
ask: Keep payment stablecoins and tokenized deposits out of "funds" unless held under stated conditions
text: Keep payment stablecoins and tokenized deposits out of "funds" unless held under stated conditions. The SEC asks whether stablecoins and tokenized deposits can be the funds a transfer agent holds for issuers and securityholders. A token held for securityholders carries risks a deposit account does not: loss of keys, an issuer's freeze or redemption halt, and network failure. Permit them to stand in for funds only if they are payment stablecoins of permitted payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, or deposit liabilities of a depository institution recorded on a crypto network; they are held by a bank or trust company in a for-the-benefit-of wallet, not by the transfer agent itself; the transfer agent keeps per-client records and reconciles them to the wallet's balance on the network at least every business day; and the business continuity plan addresses a freeze or redemption halt by the issuer. Segregate tokens the transfer agent holds for securityholders, such as undelivered distributions, from its own assets on the same terms the rule applies to funds.

letter_title: SEC Transfer Agent Rules
ask: Make tokenization visible on Form TA-2
text: Make tokenization visible on Form TA-2. The form's proposed new question counts the issues for which a registrant kept the master securityholder file using distributed ledger technology "in whole or in part," a count that lumps a ledger that is the whole official record with one that is only a component of it and misses a ledger that only copies it, and no question links an issue to the network that carries its record. Split that question into issues for which the ledger is the file, a component of it, or a synchronized copy; require, by issue and publicly, the network and contract address of each tokenized issue, as entries on the list of issues serviced that the amended form would already require; define the issuer-sponsored and third-party-sponsored models in the form instructions; and make the names of distributed ledger platforms and tokenization agents public. A contract address is already public on its network; the form would only connect it to the transfer agent of record, and asks for no key, wallet or holder information.
topics: disclosure and reporting measurement and data
refs: Questions 16, 19, 21 and 23; Form TA-2 Question 4(e); Form TA-2 Question 13

letter_title: SEC Transfer Agent Rules
ask: Make the wallet address part of position detail for tokenized positions, and address lost keys
text: Make the wallet address part of position detail for tokenized positions, and address lost keys. Require the wallet address, and the network, as position detail for every tokenized position, in addition to, and not instead of, the holder's name and mailing address, with procedures for changes of address and for lost keys. A wallet address shows which key can move the units; it does not show who holds them, and it fails as a way to reach the holder at the moment that matters most, when the key is lost. In the rule on lost and inactive securityholders, define the transaction limb of account activity for tokenized positions as transactions initiated or directed by, and reasonably attributable to, the holder, and not an unsolicited incoming transfer or automatic distribution alone, since on many networks anyone can send a token to any address; and treat a holder as an unresponsive payee when a payment goes to a wallet that has shown no such transaction for the inactivity period, with the written notice sent to the mailing address of record, so that the holder can be found before its property is lost.

letter_title: FinCEN A7 Network Special Measure
ask: Adopt the prohibition on transmittals of funds rather than special measures one through five
text: Adopt the prohibition on transmittals of funds rather than special measures one through five. A7A5 transfers do not pass through correspondent accounts, and special measure five reaches only correspondent and payable-through accounts, a limit the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets identified in July 2025.

letter_title: FinCEN A7 Network Special Measure
ask: Deliver Sub-Agent addresses, not only names, and state the minimum screening expected for convertible virtual currency
text: Deliver Sub-Agent addresses, not only names, and state the minimum screening expected for convertible virtual currency. A blockchain transfer carries addresses, not names. The list FinCEN shares through its FI-Portal should carry each Sub-Agent's known CVC addresses and blockchains and the A7A5 token contracts, including wrapped representations (separate tokens that stand for A7A5), in machine-readable form. The prohibition should reach a transmittal sent from or to a listed address; funds that passed through a listed address at some earlier point, and arrived from an address that is not on the list, should be handled through risk-based due diligence and suspicious activity reporting.

letter_title: FinCEN A7 Network Special Measure
ask: State what the prohibition requires of payment stablecoin issuers, which become covered financial institutions by cross-reference
text: State what the prohibition requires of payment stablecoin issuers, which become covered financial institutions by cross-reference. When FinCEN's pending issuer rule is final, permitted payment stablecoin issuers will become covered institutions under this rule automatically. Prohibit their primary market dealings with listed Sub-Agents (issuing, redeeming, converting, or holding stablecoins for them), require, or at least recognize as compliance, a prompt freeze of a listed address that holds their stablecoin, and state that the rule does not require blanket monitoring of secondary market transfers (transfers between other holders).

letter_title: FinCEN A7 Network Special Measure
ask: Put in the regulatory text the preamble's rule that OFAC blocking counts as compliance, and separate blocking from returning in the CVC safe harbor
text: Put in the regulatory text the preamble's rule that OFAC blocking counts as compliance, and separate blocking from returning in the CVC safe harbor. In the provision that protects an institution after it receives CVC from a Sub-Agent, state separately when to block and when to reject and return, and say what to do when return is not feasible.

letter_title: FinCEN A7 Network Special Measure
ask: Identify CVC transfers by transaction hash in the notice and records, and treat returns and freezes as permitted disclosures
text: Identify CVC transfers by transaction hash in the notice and records, and treat returns and freezes as permitted disclosures. For CVC, identify each transfer by its transaction hash, its unique public identifier, in the required notice and records, and confirm that a return transfer or an issuer freeze, both visible on the public blockchain, is a permitted disclosure even though FinCEN's list is non-public.
topics: disclosure and reporting measurement and data
